answer: My anti-Sybil design is a glacier atlas of place-bound proof. Each miner keeps an atlas page recording one nearby glacier's melt line from a dated photo they took, and the network cross-checks it against a delta downstream: meltwater sediment must match the claimed glacier's mineral signature, so a copied page fails the delta test. Sybils cannot fake both ends, since the photo needs a real visit and the sample a real riverbank, and one person can be in only one place at a time. Pages gain weight only when neighbours confirm the same melt line, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust.
